subclauses.title: Understanding the organization and its context
subclauses.summary: Identify internal and external issues that affect the ability of the ISMS to achieve its outcomes. A 2024 amendment added that climate change must be considered as a possible relevant issue.

subclauses.title: Needs and expectations of interested parties
subclauses.summary: Identify interested parties, their relevant requirements, and which of those the ISMS will address. The 2024 amendment notes that interested parties can have climate-related requirements.

subclauses.title: Determining the scope of the ISMS
subclauses.summary: Set the boundaries of the ISMS using 4.1, 4.2, and the interfaces and dependencies with other organisations. The scope must be documented.

subclauses.title: Information security management system
subclauses.summary: Establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the ISMS, including the processes it needs and how they interact.

subclauses.title: Leadership and commitment
subclauses.summary: Top management must show commitment, for example by aligning the policy with strategy, integrating the ISMS into business processes, providing resources and supporting other managers.

subclauses.title: Policy
subclauses.summary: Top management sets an information security policy that suits the organisation's purpose, includes or frames objectives, commits to meeting requirements and to continual improvement. It must be documented, communicated and available to interested parties as appropriate.

subclauses.title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
subclauses.summary: Top management makes sure responsibilities and authorities for security-relevant roles are assigned and communicated. It must specifically assign who ensures the ISMS conforms to the standard and who reports ISMS performance to top management.

subclauses.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities: general
subclauses.summary: Plan actions for risks and opportunities so the ISMS achieves its outcomes, prevents undesired effects and improves continually.

subclauses.title: Information security risk assessment
subclauses.summary: Define and apply a risk assessment process with criteria for risk acceptance and for performing assessments. Repeated assessments must give consistent, valid and comparable results. Identify risks to confidentiality, integrity and availability, assign risk owners, analyse consequences and likelihood, determine risk levels and evaluate against criteria. Keep the process documented.

subclauses.title: Information security risk treatment
subclauses.summary: Choose treatment options, determine the necessary controls, compare them with Annex A so nothing is missed, produce a Statement of Applicability, write a risk treatment plan, and get risk owners to approve the plan and accept residual risk. Keep the process documented.

subclauses.title: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
subclauses.summary: Set measurable (where practicable) objectives consistent with the policy, monitored, communicated and updated. Plan what will be done, resources, who is responsible, completion dates and how results are evaluated.

subclauses.title: Planning of changes
subclauses.summary: New in 2022. Changes to the ISMS must be carried out in a planned way.

subclauses.title: Resources
subclauses.summary: Provide the resources needed for the ISMS.

subclauses.title: Competence
subclauses.summary: Determine required competence, ensure people are competent through education, training or experience, take action to close gaps, and keep evidence of competence.

subclauses.title: Awareness
subclauses.summary: People working under the organisation's control must know the policy, their contribution to the ISMS, and the consequences of not conforming.

subclauses.title: Communication
subclauses.summary: Decide what to communicate, when, with whom and how.

subclauses.title: Documented information
subclauses.summary: Include documented information required by the standard and that the organisation decides it needs. Control creation, updating, identification, format, review, approval, distribution, access, storage, version control, retention and disposal, including external documents.

subclauses.title: Operational planning and control
subclauses.summary: Plan, implement and control the processes needed, set criteria for them, control planned changes, review unintended changes, and control externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the ISMS.

subclauses.title: Information security risk assessment
subclauses.summary: Perform risk assessments at planned intervals and when significant changes occur. Keep the results.

subclauses.title: Information security risk treatment
subclauses.summary: Implement the risk treatment plan. Keep the results.

subclauses.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
subclauses.summary: Decide what to monitor and measure, methods, when, who does it, and when and by whom results are analysed and evaluated. Keep evidence of results.

subclauses.title: Internal audit
subclauses.summary: Run audits at planned intervals to check the ISMS conforms to the organisation's own requirements and the standard, and is effectively implemented. Plan an audit programme, define criteria and scope, pick objective and impartial auditors, report results to management, and keep evidence.

subclauses.title: Management review
subclauses.summary: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals. Inputs include status of previous actions, changes in issues and interested party needs, performance feedback (nonconformities, monitoring results, audit results, objectives), interested party feedback, risk assessment results and treatment status, and improvement opportunities. Outputs include improvement decisions and any changes needed. Keep evidence.

subclauses.title: Continual improvement
subclauses.summary: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the ISMS. In the 2022 edition this subclause comes first.

subclauses.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
subclauses.summary: React to the nonconformity, control and correct it, deal with consequences, find the root cause, check whether similar issues exist or could occur, implement actions, review their effectiveness and change the ISMS if needed. Keep evidence of the nonconformity, actions taken and results.

mandatory_documented_information.note: Treated as mandatory by most certification bodies. The standard explicitly requires documented information on the treatment process and its results.

mandatory_documented_information.item: Documented information the organisation decides is necessary
Evidence that processes have been carried out as planned
Nonconformities, actions taken and corrective action results

attributes_iso27002.operational_capabilities_note: Fifteen capabilities such as governance, asset management, identity and access management, threat and vulnerability management

controls.summary: Get vulnerability information, assess exposure and act.

key_concepts.definition: Information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorised people, entities or processes.
Information is accurate and complete.
Information is accessible and usable on demand by an authorised entity.
Policies, procedures, guidelines and the related resources and activities, managed together by an organisation to protect its information assets (ISO/IEC 27000).
Effect of uncertainty on objectives. Often expressed as a combination of consequence and likelihood.
Person or entity with the accountability and authority to manage a risk.
Risk remaining after risk treatment.
The level of risk the organisation is prepared to accept. Set in the risk criteria under 6.1.2.

Commonly taught as four options: modify (apply controls), retain (accept), avoid, and share (for example insurance). ISO/IEC 27005:2018 had a subclause for each. The 2022 edition replaced these with one general clause on selecting treatment options, but sharing and retention remain defined terms.
Document listing the necessary controls, justification for including them, whether they are implemented, and justification for excluding any Annex A controls.
Non-fulfilment of a requirement.
Correction fixes the immediate problem. Corrective action removes the root cause to stop it recurring.
Person or organisation that can affect, be affected by, or think itself affected by a decision or activity.
Person or group that directs and controls the organisation at the highest level.
Information an organisation must control and maintain, and the medium holding it. Replaces the older terms documents and records.
The common clause structure (formerly Annex SL) shared by ISO management system standards such as 27001, 9001, 14001 and 42001. Makes integration easier.
Plan-Do-Check-Act. ISO 27001:2022 does not require or mention PDCA. By common training convention, clauses 4 to 6 map to Plan, 7 to 8 to Do, 9 to Check and 10 to Act.
Certification body reviews documentation and readiness, including scope, policy, risk process and SoA.
Certification body checks the ISMS is implemented and effective in practice.
Annual audits in years two and three of the certification cycle.
Full re-audit before the three-year certificate expires.

Annex A went from 114 controls in 14 domains to 93 controls in 4 themes. 11 controls are new. Clause 6.3 Planning of changes was added. The transition period for certified organisations ended on 31 October 2025.

questions.question: Which property is lost when an attacker alters payroll figures without being detected?
questions.explanation: Integrity concerns accuracy and completeness. Unauthorised change breaks integrity.

questions.question: A ransomware attack encrypts a file server so staff cannot open files. No data was copied out. Which property is affected?
questions.explanation: Staff cannot access or use the information, so availability is lost.

questions.question: Which standard in the 27000 family can an organisation be certified against?
questions.explanation: 27001 holds the requirements. The others are guidance.

questions.question: Where would you find the official definitions of ISMS terms?
questions.explanation: 27000 is the overview and vocabulary standard.

questions.question: What does the harmonized structure provide?
options: A common clause structure across ISO management system standards
questions.explanation: The shared structure lets organisations integrate 27001 with 9001, 42001 and others.

questions.question: Which standard provides requirements for bodies that certify ISMSs?
questions.explanation: 27006 covers certification body requirements. 27007 is audit guidance.

questions.question: How many controls are in Annex A of ISO/IEC 27001:2022?
questions.explanation: 93 controls in four themes. 114 was the 2013 figure.

questions.question: Which theme contains the most controls?
questions.explanation: Organizational has 37, Technological 34, Physical 14, People 8.

questions.question: Which clause requires top management to show leadership and commitment?
questions.explanation: 5.1 Leadership and commitment.

questions.question: Which clause was newly added in the 2022 edition?
questions.explanation: 6.3 requires changes to the ISMS to be planned.

questions.question: Which of these is a new control in 2022?
questions.explanation: 5.7 Threat intelligence is one of the 11 new controls.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a new 2022 control?
questions.explanation: 8.13 Information backup existed in 2013.

questions.question: Clause 4.2 requires the organisation to identify what?
options: Interested parties and their relevant requirements
questions.explanation: 4.2 covers needs and expectations of interested parties.

questions.question: Which item is mandatory documented information?
questions.explanation: 6.2 requires documented objectives. The others may be useful but are not explicitly required.

questions.question: Which 27002 attribute set uses Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover?
questions.explanation: These five concepts align with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions.

questions.question: Control 8.31 requires separation of which environments?
questions.explanation: 8.31 separates development, test and production.

questions.question: What did Amendment 1 (2024) add to ISO/IEC 27001:2022?
options: Climate change consideration in clauses 4.1 and 4.2
questions.explanation: The climate action amendment applied to many ISO management system standards.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a gap analysis at project start?
options: Compare current practice with ISO 27001 requirements
questions.explanation: It shows what exists and what is missing, which shapes the project plan.

questions.question: Which input should the ISMS scope consider?
options: Issues from 4.1, requirements from 4.2, and interfaces and dependencies
questions.explanation: 4.3 lists these three inputs.

questions.question: Who establishes the information security policy?
questions.explanation: 5.2 places the policy with top management.

questions.question: The risk assessment process must produce results that are:
questions.explanation: 6.1.2 requires repeated assessments to give consistent, valid and comparable results.

questions.question: Which two sets of criteria must the risk assessment process establish?
options: Risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments
questions.explanation: Both are required by 6.1.2.

questions.question: Why is management authorisation obtained before implementation?
options: It is an Annex A control
To confirm commitment, resources and acceptance of the plan
questions.explanation: Formal sign-off secures resources and shows the leadership commitment 5.1 requires.

questions.question: Information security objectives must be:
options: Measurable where practicable and consistent with the policy
questions.explanation: 6.2 sets this requirement.

questions.question: A project charter for an ISMS project should mainly define:
options: Objectives, scope, sponsor, roles, resources and milestones
questions.explanation: The charter authorises and frames the project.

questions.question: Which risk treatment option is insurance an example of?
questions.explanation: Insurance transfers part of the consequence to a third party.

questions.question: An organisation stops offering a risky online service. Which option is this?
questions.explanation: Ending the activity removes the risk source.

questions.question: The SoA must contain:
options: Necessary controls, justification for inclusion, implementation status, and justification for excluding Annex A controls
questions.explanation: 6.1.3 d sets these contents.

questions.question: Why must the organisation compare its controls with Annex A?
options: Every Annex A control is mandatory
To check no necessary controls are overlooked
questions.explanation: Annex A is a checklist. Controls can be excluded with justification.

questions.question: Who approves the risk treatment plan?
questions.explanation: Risk owners approve it and accept residual risk under 6.1.3.

questions.question: Clause 7.3 Awareness requires people to know:
options: The policy, their contribution, and consequences of not conforming
questions.explanation: These three points form 7.3.

questions.question: When must risk assessments be repeated under 8.2?
options: At planned intervals and when significant changes occur
questions.explanation: Both triggers are required.

questions.question: Which control best addresses an employee leaving with a company laptop?
questions.explanation: 5.11 covers recovering assets on leaving.

questions.question: Which control applies to background checks on new staff?
questions.explanation: 6.1 Screening.

questions.question: A company stores customer data in a SaaS platform. Which new control is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: 5.23 Information security for use of cloud services.

questions.question: Clause 7.5 controls documented information. Which is part of that control?
questions.explanation: 7.5.3 covers version control, retention and disposal among others.

questions.question: Internal audits must be carried out by auditors who are:
questions.explanation: 9.2 requires objectivity and impartiality, not external status.

questions.question: Which is an input to management review?
options: Results of risk assessment and status of risk treatment
questions.explanation: 9.3 lists risk assessment results and treatment status as inputs.

questions.question: What does Stage 1 of the certification audit mainly assess?
questions.explanation: Stage 1 reviews documentation and readiness. Stage 2 tests implementation.

questions.question: How often are surveillance audits normally held?
questions.explanation: Surveillance audits happen yearly between certification and recertification.

questions.question: Clause 9.1 requires the organisation to determine:
options: What to monitor and measure, methods, timing and who analyses results
questions.explanation: These are the 9.1 requirements.

questions.question: Who conducts the management review?
questions.explanation: 9.3 places the review with top management.

questions.question: Which standard gives guidance on monitoring and measurement?
questions.explanation: 27004 covers monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation.

questions.question: An auditor finds a firewall rule review was missed. The team completes the review that day. This is:
questions.explanation: Fixing the immediate issue is correction. Corrective action addresses why it was missed.

questions.question: What must happen after corrective action is implemented?
questions.explanation: 10.2 requires effectiveness review.

questions.question: In ISO/IEC 27001:2022, what is the title of clause 10.1?
questions.explanation: The 2022 edition reordered clause 10. 10.1 is Continual improvement and 10.2 is Nonconformity and corrective action. Preventive action was removed in 2013, and management review is 9.3.

questions.question: Continual improvement in clause 10.1 targets the ISMS's:
questions.explanation: 10.1 requires continual improvement of the ISMS's suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

questions.question: Why check whether similar nonconformities exist elsewhere?
options: To find wider weaknesses and prevent recurrence
questions.explanation: 10.2 requires this check as part of corrective action.

questions.question: Which PDCA stage does clause 10 represent?
questions.explanation: By convention, improvement is the Act stage. The standard itself does not mention PDCA.

questions.question: What evidence must be kept for nonconformities?
options: Nature of the nonconformity, actions taken and results of corrective action
questions.explanation: 10.2 requires this documented information.

questions.question: Which is an output of management review?
options: Decisions on improvement opportunities and any changes needed to the ISMS
The risk acceptance criteria for the first time
questions.explanation: 9.3 outputs include improvement decisions and any need for changes to the ISMS.

questions.question: Who should internal audit results be reported to?
questions.explanation: 9.2 requires results to be reported to relevant management.

questions.question: An audit programme under 9.2 must take into account:
options: The importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits
questions.explanation: Programme planning considers process importance and previous audit results.

questions.question: Which is the best example of a measurable ISMS metric under 9.1?
options: Percentage of staff completing awareness training within 30 days of joining
questions.explanation: A useful metric is specific and measurable, so trends can be analysed and evaluated.

questions.question: During Stage 2, the auditor finds a major nonconformity. What normally happens?
options: Certification is withheld until correction and corrective action are accepted
The certificate is issued with a note
questions.explanation: A major nonconformity must be addressed, with evidence accepted by the certification body, before certification is granted.

questions.question: Can an internal auditor audit their own work?
options: No, it breaches objectivity and impartiality
questions.explanation: 9.2 requires auditors who ensure objectivity and impartiality. Auditing your own work undermines both.

questions.question: Which standard gives guidance specific to auditing an ISMS?
questions.explanation: 27007 gives ISMS audit guidance, building on ISO 19011.

exam_domain_weight_note: Weights as published by TRECCERT. They add up to about 113%, so treat them as relative emphasis, not exact question counts.
